subject: [Escalation] EU production: egress network failure -> retry-loop / elevated 5xx & 429
messages:

Subject: High 5xx/429 in EU prod since 08:50 UTC

Hi team,

We're seeing a large spike in 5xx and 429 responses across our EU region since ~08:50 UTC. Latency has jumped from ~120ms to multiple seconds, and our clients are now entering retry loops which is making the problem worse. Sample request IDs: req_eu_9a1f, req_eu_9a7c, req_eu_9b20.

Can you confirm if anything changed on your side? Our SREs are holding traffic back but RetailCloud is sensitive to sustained errors for checkout traffic. This is P0 for us.

Attached: a few client-side traces (we can share more).

Thanks,
Lena

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-03-22T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 in EU prod since 08:50 UTC

Quick update from infra: we've identified a sharp increase in TCP handshake timeouts and DNS resolution failures originating from our primary EU egress POP (eu-west-3-egress-01) at ~08:49:38 UTC. Upstream provider reported packet drops on their transit link. This caused connection resets that surface as 5xx from our frontends and a transient 429 spike as internal backpressure kicked in.

Mitigations in flight (10:03 UTC):
- Shifted ~60% of EU user traffic to secondary egress POP eu-west-1-egress-02 (controlled steering).
- Deployed server-side retry-throttling (cap concurrent retries per client + add exponential backoff) at the load balancer.
- Captured PCAPs and aggregated logs (attached: pcap-20260322-eu-egress.pcap, redwood-debug-logs-20260322.tar.gz).

Preliminary impact: RetailCloud saw 5xx rate peak at 7.8% for a 12-minute window, errors are now trending down after the shift, residual 429s expected while backpressure drains.

Next: coordinating with upstream provider and considering emergency purchase of dedicated transit for critical customers if this recurs.

— Grace
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-03-22T12:45:00Z
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 in EU prod since 08:50 UTC

Heads-up for leadership decision: after the traffic shift we're stable but this is a third-party transit failure affecting multiple customers. Options we should consider (fast):
1) Engage upstream provider's premium escalation (24/7 war room) — requires exec sign-off for commitment.
2) Provision temporary dedicated transit (BGP path) for RetailCloud's EU traffic — cost estimate ~ $12k/month (short-term).
3) Offer RetailCloud a customer credit and priority routing until we implement a hardening plan.

Recommend we authorize the provider escalation (1) immediately and pre-approve the credit (3) to prevent churn. Monica, can you prepare a one-page customer summary and propose the goodwill credit (0.5–1 month)? Vivek, will escalate to PO/CS executive if you agree.

— Markus
Head of Network Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@retailcloud.com>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, support@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-22T16:02:00Z
Subject: [Resolved] EU production: egress network failure -> retry-loop / elevated 5xx & 429

Lena / RetailCloud execs — thank you for patience. Final summary and next steps: 

What happened: an upstream transit provider experienced packet drops on an EU egress path starting 08:49 UTC, producing TCP timeouts and DNS failures that surfaced as elevated 5xx and transient 429s. Client retries without jitter amplified load (retry-loop).

Impact: RetailCloud saw a 7.8% 5xx peak for ~12 minutes and increased p95 latency from ~120ms -> 3s during the window. No data loss; requests either retried or failed fast.

Immediate fixes applied:
- Traffic steering to secondary EU POP and retry-throttling at the edge (completed 10:03 UTC).
- PagerDuty incident opened: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/INC-20260322-88
- Collected PCAPs/logs and created Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-2987

Customer remediation: 
- We're offering RetailCloud a one-month credit (pro-rated) as goodwill. Monica will follow up with the exact credit amount and formal letter.
- Scheduling a postmortem w/ RetailCloud next Wednesday 9:30 UTC; invite to follow.

Longer-term actions:
- Engage provider premium escalation and get SLA commitments.
- Expand multi-POP egress coverage and test failovers quarterly.
- Implement automatic client-visible guidance and server-side soft-fail policies to reduce retry amplification.

Attachments: pcap-20260322-eu-egress.pcap, redwood-debug-logs-20260322.tar.gz, traffic-shift-screenshot.png

If you want an executive call now, I can arrange. Otherwise Monica will send the credit proposal + PM for the postmortem.

— Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
